newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. says no common ground in U.K. air talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says no common ground in U.K. air talks.

text.p: The United States and Britain have "not yet found common ground" in talks on opening their respective aviation markets, said Susan McDermott, deputy director of negotiations at the U.S. Department of Transportation.

"There is very little excuse for excluding pricing, route entry and capacity and the ability to connect with other airlines," she said in reply to questions at the 18th Air Cargo Forum meeting here on Monday.
She said the aim is "to open the market between the U.S., U.K. and the rest of the world."
Asked whether a separate U.S.-UK agreement could be reached on cargo, McDermott said,"it certainly is a very real option for us."

There has been concern in the U.S. air cargo industry that it has been caught in negotiations relating to passenger airlines but McDermott said cargo deals have been done recently with Asian countries, including Japan and it "could be done in the case of the U.S.-UK talks".
